facts.statement: A preparator named Sergio Saldivia discovered the skeleton of a new theropod dinosaur in a canyon wall in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001, Sergio Saldivia, preparator at the Museo Carmen Funes, thirty kilometres northeast of Plaza Huincul in a canyon wall discovered the skeleton of a theropod dinosaur new to science.

facts.statement: The species Murusraptor barrosaensis was formally named and described by Rodolfo Anibal Coria and Philip John Currie in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, the type species Murusraptor barrosaensis was named and described by Rodolfo Anibal Coria and Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH-411 is a partial skeleton of an immature individual dating to the Coniacian age.
facts.quote: The holotype, MCF-PVPH-411, was found in a layer of the Sierra Barrosa Formation dating from the Coniacian. It consists of a partial skeleton with skull, of an immature individual.

facts.statement: The holotype includes a partial skull with thirty-one teeth, twelve vertebrae, eleven ribs, and various limb and pelvic bones.
facts.quote: The skeletal elements recovered for this type specimen of Murusraptor include a partial skull consisting of a complete braincase with frontals and parietals, right lacrimal, prefrontal, postorbital, quadrate, pterygoid, epipterygoid and ectopterygoid, thirty-one teeth, the rear elements of the right lower jaw, twelve vertebrae from the back, sacrum and tail, eleven thoracic ribs, a single haemal arch or chevron bone, several gastralia, a third manual ungual, complete left ilium, part of a right ilium, proximal ends of both pubic bones, distal ends of the ischia, the right tibia, and a calcaneum.

facts.statement: The holotype is estimated to be 6.4 meters long, but it is an immature specimen that could have grown larger.
facts.quote: The holotype of Murusraptor is estimated to be 6.4 m, but is considered to be an immature specimen, as the cranial sutures in its braincase have not yet disappeared; this indicates it would have been potentially larger.

facts.statement: Murusraptor possessed hollow sacral ribs.
facts.quote: The sacral ribs are hollow.

facts.statement: Murusraptor has unique ischia that are short, transversely flattened, and vertically widened, a trait unique among all theropods.
facts.quote: The ischia are short, transversely flattened and vertically slightly widened. These last two traits are unequivocal autapomorphies, unique derived qualities, as they are unique within the entire Theropoda.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows severe infections on the left side of the braincase and tooth marks likely inflicted by another theropod.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Murusraptor shows signs of severe infections around the left side of its braincase. Two tooth marks, likely inflicted by another theropod, are visible in front of and below the nuchal crest on the skull.

facts.statement: Murusraptor is classified as a megaraptoran, a group of large predatory dinosaurs with disputed exact classification.
facts.quote: Murusraptor is a megaraptoran, one of a group of large predatory dinosaurs whose exact classification remains disputed.

facts.statement: Murusraptor belongs to the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: familia: Megaraptora

facts.statement: Murusraptor fossils were found in Coniacian-age Cretaceous strata in the Sierra Barrosa Formation of Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se han encontrado en estratos que datan del período Cretácico, durante el Coniaciano, en la Formación Sierra Barrosa, parte del Grupo Neuquén, en la Patagonia, Argentina, Suramérica.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was discovered in 2001 by preparator Sergio Saldivia in a canyon wall thirty kilometers northeast of Plaza Huincul.
facts.quote: En 2001, Sergio Saldivia, preparador del Museo Carmen Funes, a treinta kilómetros al noreste de Plaza Huincul en una pared del cañón, descubrió el esqueleto de un dinosaurio terópodo nuevo para la ciencia.

facts.statement: Murusraptor barrosaensis was formally named and described in 2016 by Rodolfo Aníbal Coria and Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: En 2016, la especie tipo Murusraptor barrosaensis fue nombrada y descrita por Rodolfo Aníbal Coria y Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH-411 is an incomplete skeleton including a skull that belonged to an immature individual.
facts.quote: El holotipo , MCF-PVPH-411 consiste en un esqueleto parcial con cráneo, de un individuo inmaduro.

facts.statement: The holotype includes thirty-one teeth, twelve posterior vertebrae, eleven thoracic ribs, a single chevron, various gastralia, a third manual claw, and parts of the pelvis and hindlimb bones.
facts.quote: Los elementos esqueléticos recuperados para este tipo de muestra de Murusraptor incluyen un cráneo parcial que consiste en una caja cerebral completa con frontales y parietales, lagrimal derecho, prefrontal, postorbital, cuadrado, pterigoideo, epipterigoideo y ectopterigoideo, treinta y un dientes, los elementos posteriores del derecho mandíbula inferior, doce vértebras desde la parte posterior, sacro y cola, once costillas torácicas, un solo arco hemal o hueso de cheuron, varias gastralia, un tercer ungual manual, ilion izquierdo completo, parte de un ilion derecho, extremos proximales de ambos huesos púbicos, extremos distales del isquion, la tibia derecha y un calcáneo.

facts.statement: The genus name Murusraptor combines the Latin words for "wall" and "thief," referring to the canyon wall discovery site, while the species name refers to the Sierra Barrosa locality.
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva de la palabra murus, que es un término en latín para "pared", refiriéndose a que el espécimen fue hallado en la pared de un cañón, mientras que el término latino raptor significa "ladrón"; "barrosaensis", el nombre de la especie, alude a la Sierra Barrosa, la localidad donde fue recogido el espécimen.

facts.statement: Murusraptor is classified as a megaraptoran, a group of large predatory dinosaurs whose exact classification remains debated.
facts.quote: Murusraptor es un megarraptorano, miembro de un grupo de grandes dinosaurios depredadores cuya clasificación exacta permanece en discusión.

facts.statement: Megaraptorans have been classified variously as dromaeosaurids, allosauroid carnosaurs, or tyrannosauroid coelurosaurs.
facts.quote: Alguna vez considerados como dromeosáuridos, han sido clasificados tanto como carnosaurios alosauroideos como celurosaurios tiranosauroideos.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen shows signs of severe infections around the left side of its braincase.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Murusraptor muestra signos de infecciones graves alrededor del lado izquierdo de su caja cerebral.

facts.statement: Two tooth marks, likely inflicted by another theropod, are visible on the skull in front of and below the nuchal crest.
facts.quote: Dos marcas de dientes, probablemente infligidas por otro terópodo, son visibles delante y debajo de la cresta nucal en el cráneo.

facts.statement: Severe infections caused the entire left side of the skull's occiput to become deformed.
facts.quote: Debido a las infecciones, todo el lado izquierdo del occipucio , la parte posterior de la cabeza, estaba deformado.

facts.statement: Some of the ribs were also infected.
facts.quote: Algunas de las costillas también estaban infectadas.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether these infections contributed to the death of the theropod.
facts.quote: Se desconoce si esto contribuyó o no a la muerte del terópodo.

facts.statement: Murusraptor lived during the Coniacian stage, approximately 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Coniacian (89.8 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Zurriaguz, Baiano, and Coria investigated the pneumaticity of the postcranial bones of Murusraptor barrosaensis.
facts.quote: A study on the pneumaticity of bones of the postcranial skeleton of Murusraptor barrosaensis is published by Zurriaguz, Baiano & Coria (2026).
